decisions.text: WebSummit testers are the team's phones on internal TestFlight (Gerard, Dave, Rikki and other App Store Connect users): no Beta App Review. Android testers install the EAS preview APK by link. No Play Console exists yet; Play answers are drafted for later.
The app deletes nothing: no account or workspace deletion. Deleting a workspace stays in Studio; a login is removed through support, as the privacy policy says.

No pointer to creating an account anywhere in the app (no 'Create an account', 'Sign up', 'No account?'): both stores count a link out to sign-up as account creation, which would require in-app deletion.
Nothing about plans, credits or prices; a paused workspace says 'Your workspace is paused; ask your workspace owner'.

The app never says 'nothing leaves your server' or anything as broad: even paired to a self-hosted install it sends crash reports to Automatos's Sentry, checks Expo for updates and, if the operator agrees, sends push through Expo and Apple or Google.
The one-time AI-provider consent sheet names every provider ai_providers lists, Retell AI included when the workspace can use Auto Live.

Report this on Auto's messages and on Deliverables (reason, optional note); on hosted Studio it reaches the workspace owner and Automatos's moderation inbox, on a self-hosted install its operator only.
Minimum age 16 (store metadata, Terms, privacy policy). The live Terms v2.3 say 18: an OWNER conflict, never resolved by this kit.

Crash and error reporting through Sentry's free developer plan in the EU region, with chat text, question text, push payloads and call ids scrubbed before sending; listed in the privacy policy, App Privacy and Data safety.
Expo 'enhanced push security' stays OFF on the EAS project (self-hosted push depends on it); a CI check fails if it is switched on.
runtimeVersion policy 'fingerprint'; a native change costs an iOS build from the 15 a month the two apps share, so native changes are batched.
The 'testflight' GitHub environment (EXPO_TOKEN) serves main only.

Gerard's VPS demo install serves WebSummit; the same VPS can serve App Review with a long-lived review pairing code, and a SaaS demo account is still needed at submission because the app offers hosted sign-in too.
No WebView anywhere; legal pages and Studio links open in the system browser.

A7 runs last and alone, on origin/main after A0–A6 merged (the launcher checks each wave's kit json on the base: present, every story passes). No dependency change, ever. app.json may change only at expo.ios.privacyManifests and expo.android.allowBackup, in ONE story (US-021f), and only where the merged base lacks them (the lead may have moved them into the foundation before its first native build). That commit's body starts 'NATIVE CHANGE:' because the merge costs one iOS build through the fingerprint loop. The gate compares app.json minus those two keys with the base, byte for byte after jq -S.

Every store requirement the code can prove is a vitest test that reads the repository (src/release/__tests__/*.test.ts, scripts/__tests__/release-*.test.ts), so CI keeps enforcing it after this wave on every later PR. App-wide audits read the WHOLE merged product tree (src/ and app/, excluding src/core/web/**, tests and fixtures), not only this wave's lines: they may be red on the base by design, and the story makes them green. Test-only helpers live in src/release/__tests__/support/ and never ship in the bundle.

An audit finding is fixed in the same story when it fits the session (an AUDIT FIX note per file, with a test that would have caught it). A finding that does not fit becomes an appended story P001R-AF-n (same shape as these stories: id, prdStory 'audit', title, description with file:line evidence, acceptanceCriteria with the cause, the change, the test and the checks, files, seams, priority after the last story, passes false, notes ''), committed with the finding story's marks; the build loop picks it up next. Never weaken an audit to make the base pass; an exception is an entry in the audit's ALLOWED list with file, text and reason.

A human step (App Store Connect, Play Console, Sentry, EAS or Clerk dashboard, a device check, a store answer) is an acceptance criterion that starts 'OWNER —'. The build session writes the exact text or values it needs under docs/release/ and marks the AC '→ OWNER — <doc path> (OT-Rn)', never DONE. Every other AC is marked '→ DONE — <evidence>'. The ownerTest list carries the same steps for the PR body.

Crash reporting policy, so the labels can say Crash Data collected and NOT linked, Performance Data and Product Interaction NOT collected: Sentry starts only with an EU DSN (host ending '.ingest.de.sentry.io') from EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN, and only while the user's 'Send crash reports' switch is on (default ON; off → nothing is sent, Sentry.close()). sendDefaultPii false; never Sentry.setUser, and beforeSend deletes event.user; no tracing (tracesSampleRate 0, enableAutoPerformanceTracing false, enableUserInteractionTracing false); no screenshots, view hierarchy or replays; enableCaptureFailedRequests false; no Sentry.wrap (its touch boundary records taps) and no navigation integration (screen names); console, touch and navigation breadcrumbs dropped, HTTP breadcrumbs reduced to method, path template and status; every message passes a redactor (tokens, keys, emails, URLs with a host, UUIDs, long quoted runs). 'Prevent storing of IP addresses' and the data scrubber are Sentry project settings: OWNER (OT-R1). Native crash events are written by the native SDKs and do not pass JS beforeSend; they carry the JS breadcrumbs already scrubbed at add time, and OWNER checks the first one (OT-R1).

decisions.text: One module, src/release/legal-links.ts, holds the public URLs the app and the store listings share: https://automatos.app/privacy, https://automatos.app/terms and https://automatos.app/contact (support). They are product constants like the bundle id, not per-environment config (the academy's src/settings/policyLinks.ts pattern); a self-hosted install's own policy is its operator's (privacy draft §11). They open in the system browser.

One registry, src/storage/secure-registry.ts, lists every expo-secure-store key the app writes, each marked userBound (cleared at sign-out and Forget this server) and survivesReinstall. On the first launch after an install (the install marker in MMKV is missing: MMKV is deleted with the app, the iOS Keychain is not) every key is deleted except survivesReinstall ones, before anything reads them. Kit default: the install id is the ONLY survivor (a random number with no personal data, so a reinstalled iPhone keeps its row in Studio, as the connect kit designed); docs/release/privacy-facts.md gives Gerard the policy sentence that says so. Every item uses a THIS_DEVICE_ONLY keychain class.
No analytics, advertising, attribution or tracking SDK; no App Tracking Transparency; NSPrivacyTracking false and no tracking domains; @sentry/react-native is the only crash or error SDK.
Every minimum-age statement the kit writes or audits says 16 (docs/release, app copy). The live Terms' 18 is listed for Gerard (OT-R13), never edited here.

The evaluated Android manifest's uses-permission set equals docs/release/android-permissions.json's allowed list exactly (a plugin that adds a permission fails CI), and its denied list (READ_MEDIA_*, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, location, contacts, overlay, foreground-service types) is absent. The iOS usage keys equal docs/release/ios-usage-keys.json; a key for an unused framework is an honest notice. The real IPA is scanned before each first submit of a native build (scripts/release/scan-ipa.mjs), because remote CocoaPods are not in node_modules.

The GraphQL field it reads is taken from Expo's published eas-cli schema, never guessed.

Everything outside this worktree is READ ONLY: the reports and drafts, the earlier kits' copies in the automatos-go checkout, the automatos-ai worktree (read origin/main with git show), the academy template, node_modules. No network call except US-021n's one schema read; no request to Sentry, Expo, Apple, Google or Clerk from this machine.

Purpose used: NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality only. Accessed-API categories: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp, …SystemBootTime, …DiskSpace, …ActiveKeyboards, …UserDefaults. The first native build proves Apple accepts them (OT-R4).

Not in this wave: a store submission, an EAS build or update, store screenshots (Gerard's phone, OWNER), a Play listing (D10), account deletion (D63), background voice (D33), backend changes (a long-lived review pairing code needs PRD-266 work: an open question), new features.
